canonical_statement: CAP-IT was a multicenter, randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled 2×2 factorial noninferiority trial conducted at 28 UK hospitals and 1 hospital in Ireland.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: multicenter, randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled, 2 × 2 factorial, noninferiority trial

canonical_statement: Eligible children were older than 6 months, weighed 6 to 24 kg, had clinically diagnosed community-acquired pneumonia, and were planned for amoxicillin monotherapy at discharge.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Children were eligible if they were older than 6 months of age, weighed 6 to 24 kg, were clinically diagnosed with CAP

population.label: Children with clinically diagnosed CAP planned for amoxicillin monotherapy at discharge

canonical_statement: Major exclusions included more than 48 hours of uninterrupted prior beta-lactam therapy or prior non-beta-lactam therapy, severe chronic disease, amoxicillin contraindication, complicated pneumonia, and bilateral wheezing without focal chest signs.

canonical_statement: Of 824 randomized children, 814 received at least one trial dose and formed the analysis population; median age was 2.5 years (IQR 1.6-3.7), 52% were male, 73% were discharged directly from the ED, and 27% had an inpatient stay under 48 hours.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Ten children received no trial medication and were excluded from the analysis, resulting in an analysis population of 814.

canonical_statement: The primary endpoint was clinically indicated nontrial systemic antibacterial treatment for respiratory tract infection, including CAP, within 28 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary end point was clinically indicated treatment with systemic antibiotics (other than trial medication) for a respiratory tract infection

concept.text: Clinically indicated antibiotic re-treatment for respiratory infection

outcome.definition: Clinically indicated systemic antibacterial treatment other than trial medication for a respiratory tract infection, including CAP, within 28 days of randomization.

canonical_statement: The noninferiority margin was an absolute risk difference of 8%, assessed against a 1-sided 95% confidence interval; 800 participants were estimated to provide 90% power assuming a 15% retreatment rate and 15% loss to follow-up.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The noninferiority margin was defined as a risk difference of 8% assessed against a 1-sided 95% CI.

canonical_statement: After pilot-phase data showed a retreatment rate near 15% rather than the originally assumed 5%, the protocol was amended to pool PED and WARD pathways and to increase the noninferiority margin from 4% to 8%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Revision of the non-inferiority margin from 4% to 8%

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that, for children with CAP discharged from an ED or hospital ward within 48 hours, lower-dose outpatient amoxicillin was noninferior to higher dose and 3-day therapy was noninferior to 7 days for subsequent antibiotic retreatment, while emphasizing severity, setting, prior antibiotics, and the noninferiority margin in interpretation.
